items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: when I was down there playing with Cab in Chu's place... he asked me did I want to come and play clarinet in his band

ctx.x: Was that a big band at the Savoy?

Well, we had about ten pieces. And this was -- in fact, when I was down there playing with Cab in Chu's place, Chick and Bardew Ali, who was his conductor, came down there one night. This is in '39, this is just before he died. And he asked me did I want to come and play clarinet in his band. I said, fine. So he said, we're going on 30 one-nighters. And you can either join now and go with us or join us when we come back. I said, well, I'll join you when you come back. And he died on that trip.
But when the band came back in town I joined the band with Ella.

items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: And Don Byases and Ben Websters, all of these fellows, Chu Berrys. Well, I played with all of them

ctx.x: I was always challenged, everywhere I went I was challenged because I was always out playing, see. And Don Byases and Ben Websters, all of these fellows, Chu Berrys. Well, I played with all of them, Lester Young -- we all went out and played at night someplace. In fact, when they used to have the sessions in Minton's (PHONETIC) I was in the house band up there. You know, there was me and Thelonious Monk and Nick Fenton and Harold West and Klock sometimes, Kenny Clark. I was in the house group.
We'll get to that a little later. But you were telling me before about the time you were about to pull out, the bus was going to Terre Haute from where? Where were you, with Moten's band?
